title: QVF Manifest
description: Canonical JSON Schema for manifest.json inside a .qvf archive (v1.1). This file is the single source of truth for the QVF contract; the vibe-view consumer loads it from a symlink so producer and consumer cannot diverge. v1.1 adds root thermochemistry/dipole/constraints metadata, an extensions governance block, and a per-section critical flag — all backward-compatible with v1. It also carries $defs/StructurePayload, which specifies the `structure` member's JSON payload. That payload is a separate archive member, so nothing in the manifest $refs it; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against the definition (QVF spec § 5.1, § 6).

qvf_version.description: QVF format version. v1 is the only released version.

schema_uri.description: Canonical URI of this JSON Schema. Informational; not validated against.

provenance.description: Optional calculation provenance carried at manifest root.

run_status.description: The archive's place in a calculation's lifecycle (QVF spec § 3.2): 'pending' = a job described (structure + job.spec) but not yet run; 'running' = a live mid-run checkpoint snapshot; 'converged' / 'failed' = a settled terminal archive. Absent means 'not stated' — a consumer MUST NOT infer a status.

bookmarks.description: Ordered camera bookmarks for consistent framing across viewers and movie export. The list order is the playback order.

thermochemistry.description: Optional thermochemical corrections at manifest root (QVF spec § 4.7).

dipole_moment.description: Optional dipole moment at manifest root (QVF spec § 4.7).

constraints.description: Optional geometry optimisation constraints at manifest root (QVF spec § 4.7).

extensions.description: Optional extension governance block declaring vendor extensions in use (QVF spec § 5.4).

Camera.description: VTK-flavoured camera. Position, focal point, and view-up are world-coordinate Cartesian (Å); the focal point is what the camera looks at, view_up is its roll axis. Projection is set by exactly one of view_angle (perspective, degrees) or parallel_scale (orthographic, world units).

ZipPath.description: Path of the member inside the zip archive. Forward slashes; no leading slash; no '..' segments.

id.description: Unique identifier for this section within the file.

kind.description: Kind string from the QVF registry or x_<vendor>.* namespace.

critical.description: If true, a consumer that does not support this kind MUST refuse to open the archive (QVF spec § 5.5).

StructureAtom.description: One atom of a `structure` payload. `position` is Cartesian, in Ångström — real coordinates, never fractional. Producers may add further per-atom fields; consumers ignore what they don't understand. Biomolecular producers conventionally add `atom_name` (PDB cols 13-16, e.g. "CA"), `residue_name` (cols 18-20), `residue_seq` (cols 23-26), `chain_id` (col 22) and `b_factor` (cols 61-66); of these only `b_factor` is typed here, because the other four predate this schema and archives in the wild carry `residue_seq` both as an integer and as a string.

b_factor.description: Per-atom temperature factor / pLDDT-style confidence (PDB cols 61-66). The per-atom carrier is authoritative over the section-level `b_factors` array, because it cannot desynchronize from its own atom (QVF spec § 5.1).

Lattice3x3.description: Lattice as three ROW vectors in Ångström: row i is the lattice vector of axis i, paired with pbc[i].

StructurePayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `structure` section's `structure` member (conventionally `structure/structure.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. `pbc` is the normative carrier of per-axis periodicity; `dimensionality` is a derived convenience. See QVF spec § 5.1.

pbc.description: Per-axis periodicity: axis i is periodic iff pbc[i]. REQUIRED when `lattice_vectors` is a non-null array; absent means a molecule ([false, false, false]). All eight patterns are legal — the periodic axes need NOT be the leading ones.

lattice_vectors.description: REQUIRED (non-null) when any pbc[i] is true; null or absent for a molecule. For every axis i with pbc[i] false, row i is non-physical bookkeeping — producers keep the matrix full-rank 3x3 so integrals and symmetry finders always see a 3-D lattice. Such a row is not a cell edge: a consumer MUST NOT draw it, replicate along it, or read it as a vacuum extent.

dimensionality.description: Derived count of periodic axes: equal to the number of true entries in `pbc`. Optional, and MUST agree when present. It carries no axis identity — a consumer MUST NOT infer WHICH axes are periodic from it.

allOf.$comment: A non-null lattice means the producer is describing a cell, so `pbc` must say which of its axes are periodic.
Conversely, a periodic axis needs the lattice vector that spans it.
dimensionality == sum(pbc), enumerated over 0..3 because JSON Schema counts matching items with minContains/maxContains rather than summing them.

BiomoleculeResidue.description: One residue of a biomolecular `structure` section. `atom_indices` are 0-based indices into the `structure` member payload's `atoms` array. Residues are listed in chain order — the order a consumer draws a ribbon in — not sorted by `seq`, because insertion codes and non-monotonic numbering are both legal and sorting would silently reorder them. See QVF spec § 5.1.

seq.description: Residue sequence number (PDB cols 23-26). Not unique across a solvated system: PDB numbering is four columns wide and wraps at 9999, so a consumer MUST NOT use it as a global key.

chain.description: Chain id this residue belongs to; matches an entry of the section's `chains` when that is present.

atom_indices.description: 0-based indices into the structure payload's `atoms` array.

BiomoleculeSecondaryStructure.description: One inclusive secondary-structure range on one chain. A producer knows things a consumer cannot infer from CA geometry alone (alpha vs pi vs 3-10 helix, beta bridge vs sheet), so a consumer that also has its own geometric assignment MUST prefer these ranges where they are supplied (QVF spec § 5.1).

start_seq.description: First residue `seq` of the range, inclusive.

end_seq.description: Last residue `seq` of the range, inclusive.

SectionStructure.description: Atoms plus an optional cell. The `structure` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/StructurePayload`; because it is an archive member rather than manifest content, a validator checks it separately from manifest.json (QVF spec § 5.1, § 6). The optional biomolecule fields (`chains`, `residues`, `secondary_structure`, `b_factors`) sit on this section object rather than in the payload, and are independently optional: a structure carrying none of them is a valid plain structure, and a consumer that does not understand them ignores them.

chains.description: Chain ids present in this structure, in the order a consumer should present them. OPTIONAL and additive.

residues.description: Residue decomposition of the structure, in chain order. OPTIONAL and additive. A consumer that can also derive residues from per-atom fields MUST prefer these when present.

secondary_structure.description: Per-chain secondary-structure ranges. OPTIONAL and additive; takes precedence over a consumer's own geometric assignment.

b_factors.description: One temperature factor per atom, parallel to the `structure` payload's `atoms` order. OPTIONAL and additive. A consumer MUST ignore the array entirely when its length differs from the atom count, rather than assigning a partial mapping; and per-atom `StructureAtom.b_factor`, where present, wins over this array.

SectionVolumeGeneric.description: Generic scalar field — escape hatch for any volumetric kind that doesn't map onto density/orbital/spin/elf/difference. Structurally identical: grid + data. Producers should prefer a more specific kind when one fits.

SectionVolumeDifference.description: Difference density (or any difference scalar field). Structurally identical to volume.density; carries optional references to the two operand sections used to compute it. Sign convention: data = a - b.

operand_a.description: Section id of the minuend (the 'a' in a - b). Must reference a section that exists in this archive.

operand_b.description: Section id of the subtrahend (the 'b' in a - b). Must reference a section that exists in this archive.

SectionVolumePotential.description: Electrostatic potential grid — identical member structure to volume.density (grid + data). Data is in hartree/e (atomic units of potential). Specified at design_qvf_format.md § 4.10.

SectionVolumeRDG.description: Reduced density gradient for NCI analysis — identical member structure to volume.density (grid + data). Data is dimensionless. Specified at design_qvf_format.md § 4.11.

SectionReactionPath.description: Self-contained reaction path: frames + per-frame energies + waypoint annotations identifying reactant / transition state / intermediate / product frames. Binary layout matches `trajectory` so the same readers can decode coords. Optional per-frame volumetric data (electron density / an orbital morphing along the path) may be attached via the `frame_volumes` (4D: [n_emitted_frames, nx, ny, nz]) + `volume_grid` members; the metadata then carries `volume_frame_index` (which path frame each emitted slab belongs to, for decimation), `volume_label`, and optional `volume_isovalue`. Readers that don't understand these members ignore them.

ReactionPathLattice.description: Per-frame lattice vectors as a binary member. Convention matches `vibeqc.PeriodicSystem.lattice`: 3x3 matrix with columns = a, b, c, in bohr. Shape is either [3, 3] when every frame shares the same lattice (the fixed-cell common case — recommended) or [n_frames, 3, 3] when frames carry per-frame lattices (forward-compat with variable-cell scans). When this member is absent the reaction.path is a molecular trajectory and renderers must draw no cell. Presence of this member — not the manifest version — is how a consumer detects a periodic reaction path.

SectionScanSurface.description: 2D relaxed-scan energy surface: two driven internal coordinates (axis_a x axis_b) with the relaxed energy at each grid node. `energies` is a 2D binary array [nA, nB]; `axis_a` / `axis_b` are the 1D coordinate values (bohr for bonds, radians for angles/dihedrals). The metadata carries per-axis label + unit. Optional `geometries` (4D-flattened [nA*nB, n_atoms, 3] in angstrom, row-major over (a, b)) lets a viewer show the relaxed structure at a clicked node.

SectionReactionWaypoints.description: Lightweight waypoint annotations layered onto an existing `trajectory` section. Use this when the frames are already carried by a trajectory and you only want to label reactant/TS/intermediate/product frames without duplicating coords.

trajectory_ref.description: Section id of the trajectory section this annotation refers to. Must reference an existing section with kind 'trajectory' in this archive.

SectionSpectraEPR.description: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR / ESR) parameters. Like spectra.nmr, the payload is a single object-shaped `spectrum` JSON member rather than a frequency/intensity pair; it carries the g-tensor, per-nucleus hyperfine (A) tensors, and the zero-field-splitting (D) tensor. The field vocabulary is intentionally loose in v1 while producer conventions settle.

SectionWavefunctionGTO.description: Atom-centered Gaussian basis + MO coefficients. Renderer-friendly: a re-sampling viewer can evaluate any orbital on its own grid (Molden-style). Complex Bloch coefficients are stored as float64 [n_mo, n_ao, 2] with last axis [real, imag].

SectionBands.description: Band structure — eigenvalues along a k-path, with optional Mulliken character projections (fat bands).

SectionBondOrders.description: Bond-order table — Mayer / Wiberg bond orders with atom-pair labels and distances. Specified at design_qvf_format.md § 4.15.

CitationsReferences.description: BibTeX bytes are carried as a binary member; consumers decode as UTF-8.

OpaqueBinaryMember.description: Opaque bytes carried as a binary member with no dtype/shape. The owning section kind defines the payload's encoding (e.g. UTF-8 text for run.record input/log).

SectionRunRecord.description: Self-contained record of one program invocation: the verbatim input handed to a quantum-chemistry code and/or the full log/output it produced, plus auxiliary attachments. `program` names the code the input/log belong to — which may differ from the root `source.program` when the archive was written by a converter. `input` and `log` are opaque binary members that MUST decode as UTF-8 text; `attachment.*` members carry arbitrary bytes described by the optional `files` index.

program.description: The program that consumed `input` / produced `log` (e.g. 'vibe-qc', 'orca'). Lowercase identifiers recommended.

command.description: Command line used to launch the run, as one string.

sequence.description: Ordering index when an archive carries multiple run records (multi-step workflows).

SectionJobSpec.description: Declarative specification of the calculation an archive requests — before, and independent of, any results it carries (QVF spec § 5.9). Together with a `structure` section it makes the archive an executable input: a runner reconstructs the job from the `spec` payload, executes it, and writes results plus a `run.record` back into the same container. The payload is declarative data, never code.

JobSpecPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `job.spec` section's `spec` member (conventionally `job_spec/spec.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. The root is open for forward growth, but engine-specific keywords SHOULD live under `options`, keeping the typed top level portable across codes (QVF spec § 5.9).

job_type.description: Which class of engine runs the job. Periodicity of the geometry itself is carried by the structure section's pbc/lattice_vectors; job_type selects the runner, it does not restate periodicity.

method.description: Method identifier (e.g. 'rhf', 'rks', 'ccsd(t)', 'gfn2'). Producer-neutral lowercase recommended. Absent means the engine's default.

charge.description: Net charge. Absent means 0. Authoritative for the job — never inferred from the structure.

kpoints.description: [n1, n2, n3] Monkhorst-Pack mesh. Periodic jobs only.

tasks.description: Ordered task identifiers, e.g. ['single_point'], ['optimize', 'hessian']. Absent means a single point.

options.description: Additional engine-specific keywords (JSON-safe values). A runner that does not recognize an option MUST refuse the job rather than silently drop it.

SectionBasisAO.description: Basis-function visualisation — one atomic orbital (contracted shell or individual primitive) evaluated on a 3-D grid. The `ao_metadata` object carries per-function quantum numbers and provenance; the `grid` + `data` members follow the same contract as all volume.* sections.

angular_momentum.description: [l, m]. Element 0 is always the shell's angular momentum l. Element 1 is the real-spherical-harmonic index m in [-l, +l] and is meaningful ONLY when `cartesian_powers` is absent; when `cartesian_powers` is present the component is a Cartesian monomial with no magnetic quantum number, element 1 is 0 by convention, and a consumer MUST ignore it. See spec Appendix A.3.

cartesian_powers.description: [lx, ly, lz] powers of the Cartesian monomial this AO is, with lx+ly+lz == angular_momentum[0]. Present if and only if the AO is a component of a Cartesian (`pure: false`) shell, which has (l+1)(l+2)/2 components rather than 2l+1 and therefore no m. Absent for spherical AOs.

SectionEquationOfState.description: Equation of state — volume-energy data points and fitted EOS parameters. Specified at design_qvf_format.md § 4.14.

SectionFermiSurface.description: Fermi surface — 3D k-space energy grid near E_F for metallic periodic systems. Specified at design_qvf_format.md § 4.12.

SectionPhononBands.description: Phonon band structure — q-path and phonon frequencies along a Brillouin-zone path. Specified at design_qvf_format.md § 4.13.

SectionPhononDOS.description: Phonon density of states — frequency grid and total phonon DOS. Specified at design_qvf_format.md § 4.13.

SectionTopologyQTAIM.description: QTAIM topological analysis — critical points and bond paths from electron-density topology. Specified at design_qvf_format.md § 4.16.

SectionVendor.description: Vendor-namespace section. The `kind` must start with `x_<vendor>`; member shape is unconstrained except that every member is a valid JsonMember or BinaryMember.

Thermochemistry.description: Thermochemical corrections at manifest root (QVF spec § 4.7). All energy quantities in Hartree.

DipoleMoment.description: Dipole moment at manifest root (QVF spec § 4.7).

origin.description: Reference point for the dipole: a conventional name for legacy producers, or an explicit 3-vector in bohr.

frozen_atoms.description: Zero-based indices of atoms frozen during optimisation.

Extensions.description: Extension governance block. Maps vendor namespace prefix (without x_ — the x_ is implied from section kinds) to its version, optional schema URI, and critical flag (QVF spec § 5.4).
